newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: BOK continues to intervene to support won -dealers.
newsitem.headline: BOK continues to intervene to support won -dealers.

text.p: South Korea's central Bank of Korea (BOK) stepped again into the interbank market in late morning trading to boost the won against the dollar, dealers said.
The central bank sold dollars at around the 830.00 level, they said.
"The central bank seems to want to keep the dollar below the 830 level," said a foreign bank dealer.
Earlier in the morning, the won weakened to 830.30, the lowest level seen since South Korea introduced a market average system in March 1990.
After the intervention, the won was trading at around 829.10.
